flag: No pass-rate floor, latency budget or value per point was declared before the run, and no configuration served as a control. The lean below is the analyst's, not a rule.
headline: Pass rate is cheap up to {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} and dear after it, where a point costs {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month; with no floor or latency budget declared, where to stop is the owner's call.
lede: One retry raises pass rate at every model and reasoning level for little cost, and Atlas-M is beaten by a cheaper Brisk-S configuration everywhere but its most expensive setting. A pass-rate floor above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} or a p95 budget under {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} would move the lean.

caveats.material_if: only if the owner would pay for the steps above the lean: each adds under a point of pass rate and nothing shows it is more than noise. The steps up to the lean are larger.
only if the lean's edge over its neighbours is the reason to choose it: picked as the knee of {n_candidates|int} configurations, its estimate is the optimistic one.
only if the check fails plans the product would accept, as on ambiguous names, where a clarifying question is the only pass.
only if the choice rests on the monthly dollar amounts rather than the order of the options: whether the declared volume counts tasks or planner calls is not stated.

decision.text: Up to {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, a point of pass rate costs at most {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month. The two steps above it buy under a point each, at {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a point, and lengthen the p95 tail.

The lean is the cheapest option for any pass-rate floor above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} and up to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean}. Above that the cheapest is {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, and above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.mean} only {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} qualifies. A p95 budget under {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} rules the lean out.

Ours, not a declared rule: {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.low.r1} a month. It is the best option for any value of a point between {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month.
A declaration from the planner's owner: a pass-rate floor and a p95 budget, or a monthly value for one point of pass rate. Either one picks the band and turns the trade into a decision.
Multi-hop is the lean's weakest task, at {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}, and its failure there collapses two hops into one query.

claims.text: Pass rate climbs steeply with cost up to {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} and flattens after it: the next point costs {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month, against {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} for the last one before it.

evidence.caption: Every configuration's pass rate against its cost per call, cost on a log axis. The upper-left edge is the frontier: from Nano-XS through {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} and {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} to {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}.

claims.text: One retry raises pass rate at every model and reasoning level, most where the base is weakest: on Nano-XS with reasoning off it adds {price.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.gain|abs|pts} points for {price.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap} a month.

evidence.caption: Model by reasoning level and retry. Each tile holds pass rate, cost per call and p95 latency; each retry column sits right of its no-retry pair.

claims.text: Atlas-M reaches the frontier only at its top setting: each of its other five is matched or beaten by a cheaper Brisk-S configuration, and the top one adds {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.gain|abs|pts} points over {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} for {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap} more a month.

evidence.caption: Atlas-M and Brisk-S configurations only, cost on a log axis. Every Atlas-M point but {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} has a Brisk-S point above and to its left.

claims.text: The dearer options are slower in the tail: {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} has a p95 of {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95}, against {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} for {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}.

evidence.caption: Latency from p50 to p95 for the four frontier options a decider would weigh. No budget was declared, so no line is drawn.

claims.text: Multi-hop is the weakest task for all four options; {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} passes {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} of it.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the four options. Descriptive: no interval, and task sizes are not stated.

claims.text: The lean's failures are planning slips a fix could target: a second hop folded into the first, a date window off by a day, and an ambiguous name answered without asking.

evidence.caption: Every failure card the snapshot holds for {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, one per task. The snapshot chose them, not the size of each task's loss.

explore.binds: Which configurations qualify, and so the cheapest one that does.
explore.outcome: Up to {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.mean} a Nano-XS setting is cheapest, and up to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} it is {arm:brisk-s.low.r0}. Above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} and up to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} the lean is. Above that {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} is, and above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.mean} only {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} qualifies.

Under {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} the lean is out. Under {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} every Atlas-M setting is out as well. No budget above {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95} binds anything.

explore.control: Monthly value of one point of pass rate
explore.outcome: The lean is best between {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}. {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} is best up to {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, and {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} above it.

omitted.what: Code's dominance call naming Nano-XS with reasoning off and no retry dominant
omitted.why: It ranks on cost alone because no quality axis was declared, and that configuration has the lowest pass rate; Method says why the report reads the pass-rate frontier instead.
Reasoning lowers it and retry raises it slightly; it feeds cost, which is shown, and changes no option's place on the frontier.
The snapshot lists them but holds no figures for any configuration.

omitted.what: Brisk-S at low reasoning with no retry
omitted.why: It sits on the cost and pass-rate edge but is best at no value of a point; it matters only under a p95 budget between its tail and the lean's, which the explore control covers.

omitted.what: Task-level pass rates for the other fourteen configurations
omitted.why: Multi-hop is weakest in each of them too; the lattice and appendix hold them, and they change no call.
It belongs to a configuration off the decider's shortlist; retry recovering truncated output is already shown by the retry claim.

omitted.what: Price rows for options off the frontier beyond the first page
omitted.why: Each is dominated by a cheaper option on pass rate; the lattice shows every one.

next.text: The planner's owner declares a pass-rate floor and a p95 latency budget, or a monthly value for one point of pass rate.
next.settles: Which band applies, which turns the trade into a decision.

next.text: Rerun {arm:nano-xs.high.r1}, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} and {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} paired on the same cases, with an interval on each difference.
next.settles: Whether the steps either side of the lean are real or noise; the gain above it is under a point and carries no interval.

next.text: Target the lean's slips, with a bounds check on date windows and a prompt that plans each hop separately, then rerun it.
next.settles: Whether the lean closes part of its gap to {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} at its own price, which would make the dearer steps harder to justify.

next.text: State whether the declared monthly volume of {meta.volume_per_month|int} counts tasks or planner calls.
next.settles: The monthly dollar figures; the order of the options does not depend on it.

method.text: Each configuration ran {scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases|int} cases, none lost or failed. Repeats and task sizes are not stated.

The campaign does not define what makes a planned call pass. The failure cards count missing calls, wrong arguments, wrong tools and malformed output as failures, and on ambiguous names only a clarifying question passes.
None. Every pass rate is a point estimate with no interval or correction, so no difference between configurations is tested.
Arithmetic on point estimates: the extra monthly cost of the next frontier option divided by the points it adds. It describes; it does not infer.
Cost is per planner call, which the lattice tiles label a reply. Monthly cost is that figure at the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month|int} a month.
p50 and p95 per configuration. Retry leaves p50 unchanged and lengthens p95.

Code's dominance computation names {arm:nano-xs.off.r0} dominant because, with no criteria declared, cost is its only axis. That configuration has the lowest pass rate, {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.off.r0.mean}, so the report reads the frontier on pass rate and cost instead.
No production configuration served as a control. Only model, reasoning level and retry were varied.
